transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, the main reason I’m here is that I'm having a really hard time at work. I'm a registered nurse, and on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. 

It’s like... an IV pump will beep, or someone asks another nurse a question nearby, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was just working on. It's happening all the time, and I really need to get it figured out.
Looking back to when you were a child, did you also have trouble staying focused or were you easily distracted?

Yes, I did. Even back in elementary school, it was a pretty big issue. My teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but careless. I was just always losing my worksheets or... completely forgetting to turn in my homework, even if I had actually finished it. 

My mom actually had to sit with me every single night while I did my schoolwork just to keep me on track and make sure I didn't wander off mentally. So, yeah, it's definitely been happening since I was little.
Do you often act impulsively or feel unusually restless, like it’s hard to stay still?

No, not really. I don't think I have a problem with that. I don't feel physically restless, and I can sit still just fine. It's really just... my mind that wanders off, not my body. So no, I wouldn't say I act impulsively or have trouble staying still.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or depressed. I mean, I get frustrated with myself at work when I lose my train of thought, but it's not like a sad or hopeless feeling. My mood is generally fine.
Outside of work, do these attention problems also cause trouble in your daily life?

Yes, it really does. I just... I forget things that should be completely routine. Like, I'll forget to call a family member back, or I'll realize I never followed up on a missing order. It happens with paying bills at home, too, or even just showing up for an appointment. 

The frustrating part is that I fully mean to do these things. Sometimes I even set a reminder on my phone, and I still somehow forget to actually do it. So, yeah, it definitely causes issues outside of work.
